To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adenosine is a safe and effective agent to use for stress echocardiography in the evaluation of patients with coronary disease.
adenosine‐induced stress echocardiography is safe, feasible, and can be performed in a wide variety of clinical scenarios.

adenosine stress echocardiography is a feasible and safe method to assess myocardial viability after thrombolytic treatment for acute myocardial infarct, to detect significant coronary artery stenoses, and to detect ischemic myocardial regions in patients with ischemic syndromes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new technique for the non‐invasive detection of coronary artery disease and assessment of myocardial viability in patients with coronary artery syndromes using adenosine echocardio graphy.
the use of adenosine as a coronary vasodilator to assess coronary artery disease.
the use of adenosine in the evaluation of ischemic syndromes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenosine stress echocardiography appears to be a promising new tool in the assessment of coronary artery disease.
adenosine stress echocardiography is a safe, effective, non‐invasive method of assessing coronary artery disease and myocardial viability.
adenosine stress echocardiography is safe and can be used to assess the physiological consequences of CAD, myocardial viability, and ischemic burden in patients with ischemic syndromes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were able to demonstrate the feasibility of performing an adenosine infusion in patients with coronary artery diseases and assess the physiological significance, myocardial viability and ischemic myocardium using echocardiography.
we can use adenosine to detect ischemic myocardial segments, assess the severity of coronary stenosis, and assess myocardium viability.
adenosine stress‐induced myocardial ischemia can be detected with echocardiography in patients with coronary artery diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adenosine stress echocardiography is a very useful tool in patients with ischemic syndromes.
adenosine stress echocardiography is a safe, feasible and useful tool to assess myocardial ischemia and viability in patients with acute coronary syndromes.
adenosine is a safe and effective pharmacological stressor that can be utilized to assess the functional significance of coronary stensoses, assess myocardial viability and detect ischemia.
